text:
julia: Quick flag 7: we saw a 15-25% tail bump on host-side CPU for small streaming requests after the KV warmup refactor landed. Traces point at parsing + tokenization hot paths.

omar: which warmup change? any repro script?

julia: warmup was kv_cache::warm_prefix_v2 in PR#4620. Repro: reproduce w/ many short messages and chunked transfer-encoding. Example: 
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/complete -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-lite\",\"input\":\"hi\"}'

lee: saw this in perf too. Flame shows: host_proto::unwrap (28%), host_tokenizer::slice (24%), kv_cache::warm_prefix_v2 (18%), grpc_flush_writev (12%), batching::heuristic_eval (10%), misc 8%.

pat: interesting that tokenizer is high. Any relation to kernel selection?

omar: yes. When batching heuristics aggregate fragmented frames we sometimes trigger early kernel fallback because token sequences look non-contiguous. The fallback path does a defensive copy which makes host tokenization heavier.

julia: root cause looks like two things happening together: 1) the refactor does a full prefix walk per-request on enqueue (synchronous), 2) ingress proxy smallwrites create many tiny buffers so warm_prefix_v2 re-scans a lot. Combined = repeated utf8/escape scans + syscall writev churn.

lee: proposal: 1) stop doing a full prefix walk on enqueue, make it connection-local and incremental; 2) tweak batching heuristic to attempt 1 round of coalesce at the ingress before per-request warmup; 3) add a tiny tokenization fast-path that assumes ascii fast-scan for small messages.

pat: for fast mitigation can we gate warm_prefix_v2 behind thresholds? e.g., skip full walk if total_bytes < 3kb && chunk_count < 4. Also emit metric parse.warm_skipped.

julia: I prototyped a skip-gate and put it behind a feature flag (runtime.feature.skip_warm_small). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4682

infra-bot: starting canary: pool=dedicated-low-latency-canary, hosts=5, image=runtime:pr-4682, ramp=45m, link=https://canary.redwood.dev/4682

omar: good. Meanwhile I'll work on incremental connection cache for prefix bytes (store first 4KB per-conn, attach sequence number). That should eliminate the repeated scans.

lee: kernel-selection note: we should record a flag when parse indicates fragmented tokens so the kernel picker prefers tolerant kernels that avoid fallback copies. Add a telemetry tag kernel.choice_reason=frag_parse.

pat: also consider reducing gRPC flush frequency for small streaming frames; we can batch flushes in the proxy with a 1-2ms coalesce window. That reduces writev syscalls.

julia: added dashboard widgets: p95/p99 parse latency, parse.warm_skipped rate, token.fastpath_rate, kernel.choice_reason breakdown. Running synthetic that simulates chat pacing.

lee: early canary numbers (10m): p95 down ~9%, p99 down ~14%, host CPU median -7%. parse.warm_skipped ~65% of small requests.

omar: promising. Next actions: 1) collect 3h of canary metrics; 2) merge incremental prefix cache (PR upcoming); 3) make batching heuristic prefer ingress coalesce before per-request warmup; 4) add unit in perf-harness to simulate fragmented chunked frames + KV warmup.

pat: PR snippet for skip gate (from PR4682):
```
// avoid full prefix walk for tiny chunked requests
if (total_bytes < 3072 && chunk_count < 4) {
  metrics.increment("parse.warm_skipped");
  return WarmResult::Skipped;
}
```

julia: filing ticket INF-1305 to track the combined work and post canary links.

infra-bot: canary live dashboard: https://canary.redwood.dev/4682 - monitoring p99, cpu, and flame snapshots.

lee: one more thought: kernel selection config should allow a lower-cost tolerant kernel for low-latency tiers; that reduces the penalty when we mis-detect contiguous tokens. I'll draft a config tweak after canary.

omar: thanks. If canary holds we'll roll the feature-flag on and land the incremental cache in a follow-up.

julia: thumbs up. Will update INF-1305 with 3h summary and flame links.

pat: nice catch everyone. :sparkles:
